newsitem.title: FRANCE: City of Rome says mulling 300 bln lira issue.
newsitem.headline: City of Rome says mulling 300 bln lira issue.

text.p: The City of Rome is considering whether to issue a munibond worth 300 billion lira and will make a decision before November, Rome's head of finance Linda Lanzillotta said on Wednesday.
"We are studying if we will do an issue," Lanzillotta told Reuters at a Paris conference.
She said no decision had been made about whether a possible issue would be in lira or a foreign currency, nor whether it would be a fixed or floating rate bond.
She said Rome wants to raise the money to help fund investment in infrastructure. "The transaction that will eventually emerge is aimed at investment the city needs to implement."
"Rome is going through a profound change and will continue to do so...clearly access to the financial markets is another small step in its economic expansion," Lanzillotta said.
So far Rome has only been rated by European rating agency IBCA, which gave the city a triple A rating. Lanzillotta said other rating agencies had approached Rome but no formal steps had been taken.

Rome launched its first munibond in July last year. It sold 100 billion lira worth of floating rate bonds to pay for new trams. It was priced at 62 basis points over the Rome Interbank Offered Rate (RIBOR).
The Italian government gave the go-ahead for a municipal and regional bond market in 1996 and Rome was the third Italian city to issue bonds.
Lanzillotta said she thought the potential size of Italian municipal bond issuance was about six billion dollars a year.
